source.title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles
source.authors: Célian Vasson; D. Ognev; Kentaro Inui; Benjamin Heinzerling

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses probes and SAE readouts to test whether variable-role information is recoverable in real code models. This bears on V4, but it does not test toy-model superposition geometry or feature competition.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported SAE-feature and SAE-reconstruction recoverability results, including comparisons with residual probes. Feature/context examples are not treated as proof of role specificity. The paper's generation interventions are not included as V4 rows because role changes and correctness under intervention do not directly measure whether SAE features recover role information.
record.test_reason: The study reads variable-role information from public SAEs on five LLMs, comparing single features, top-64 features and SAE reconstructions with residual probes. That bears on V4 (do SAEs recover sparse features carrying a concept) and on V5's completeness part (reconstructions lose information). It is not a superposition study, and residual-probe and steering results do not test any version. This is a new setting (code roles), not the toy-model method, so T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, but it omits the intervention result. Steering and removal change role annotations mostly at a correctness cost, with no clear advantage over random controls once passing tests are required.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method; it probes code-model activations and SAE representations for variable-role information.
record.method_sensitivity: Readout type, target renaming, language, implementation subtype, and observation position affect measured recoverability. Stepper AUROC is similar across the reported for-loop and other-update subsets, while thresholded recall differs.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual-stream linear probes recover role annotations (AP 0.90; counterfactual 0.813–0.877) beyond lexical baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abstract program-behaviour concepts are linearly decodable from LLM residual streams.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-feature steering and removal change role annotations but rarely with passing tests. Joint outcomes are no better than random controls (all intervals include zero).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Role-predictive SAE features do not give correctness-preserving causal control.

record.problems: The benchmark predicts automatic role annotations; extractor quality varies by role and corpus-wide precision/recall are not established. Counterfactual edits were reviewed by LLMs rather than independently adjudicated by humans or execution-verified. Evaluation uses four prescribed layers and one source-group split; renaming retains other identifiers, comments, and implementation cues. The selected-feature appendix warns that activation contexts do not establish role specificity.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-role, per-model, and per-layer plotted results in Figures 3, 7, 8, and 9 are not transcribed separately; aggregate ranges and the implementation-specific values stated in the text are recorded. Generation intervention outcomes are omitted because they measure induced role changes and correctness rather than SAE recoverability.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry.
All parts: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation.
Distribution of features across neurons. General feature inventories beyond variable roles.
Stability and canonicality of SAE features across seeds or widths. Only reconstruction completeness for one concept family is tested.
All parts: no test of multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Code-prefix surface baseline: counterfactual paired accuracy 0.750 and most-wanted-holder matched AP 0.90. These match or exceed single-feature readouts (0.622–0.713 and 0.75), which a V4 comparison needs.
missing.locator: Section 4, Matched recoverability and Counterfactual ranking paragraphs

missing.what: Single-feature AUROC by language (e.g. stepper 0.64–0.84; Figure 9b) and single-feature counterfactual accuracy by readout position (Figure 8). Declared only generally in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: The study uses SAEs mainly as a readout tool for variable roles; its bearing on superposition is indirect. Appendix O shows the best single latents encode broad concepts (extrema, booleans, loops), not roles. That fits SAEs recovering sparse features, but not role-specific ones. Counterfactual edits were LLM-reviewed only. The selected-feature results (R18–R23) come from one model and layer.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature count relative to dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity as capacity competition and the proposed dedicated-versus-shared allocation by importance.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.

The study tests recovery of code variable roles with SAE readouts in five model–SAE systems. It does not inventory general LLM features, establish that SAE features are a complete representation, or measure broad feature sharing across neurons.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of the model's representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional subspaces.

relationships.condition: Reviewed role-changing counterfactual edits and non-for-loop/Python stepper subsets
relationships.reason: Single-feature and top-64 readouts drop on edits. Selected latents fall to chance or below (0.474, 0.354, 0.536), indicating broad concept latents rather than role features. Recall falls by implementation (R9, R10, R15, R17, R19, R21, R23).
relationships.display_finding: Single-feature and top-64 readouts dropped on the edits, and selected latents fell to chance or below (0.474, 0.354, 0.536), pointing to broad concept latents rather than role features. Recall also varied by implementation.

relationships.condition: SAE reconstructions and top-64 readouts vs residual stream, five public SAEs
relationships.reason: Reconstruction probes lose 4.0–12.3 pp of counterfactual sensitivity, with CIs excluding zero, and trail residual probes on matched AUROC. The SAEs do not completely retain role distinctions (R4, R5, R8, R9).
relationships.display_finding: Probes on reconstructions lost 4.0–12.3 percentage points of counterfactual sensitivity, with confidence intervals excluding zero, and trailed residual-stream probes on matched AUROC, so role distinctions were not fully retained.

relation.reason: Its own matched, counterfactual, and reconstruction comparisons bear on V4 recoverability and V5 completeness.

tranche.reason: The study extends SAE recoverability and fidelity tests to independently defined variable roles in natural code across five model–SAE systems.

source_check.notes: R11's proposed verdict fix would substitute the full matched-Test range for an unstated native-name aggregate on the smaller renaming cohort; that substitution is unsupported. V5 evidence concerns recoverability under fixed linear fits; stability and canonicity are untested.
